solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Life form is male, hidden under newspaper?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces placed under the newspaper come after it in the answer

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical voicing a party's views
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether some creature is a man tucked away beneath a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living being, plant or animal, is a biological individual of this kind.

clue.text: Warrior in this place taking care

parts.note: here means in this place
ward means guardianship or custody, care of a minor

explanation.surface: A soldier stationed here who is looking after someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereward the Wake was the English rebel who held out against the Normans in the East Anglian fens after 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Named example: the legendary Anglo-Saxon fighter who resisted William the Conqueror.

clue.text: Treble in choir perhaps admitting solo is rubbish

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a treble singer in a church choir is typically a boy
solo means alone, on one's own: lone

explanation.surface: A choirboy allowed a solo performance turns out to be terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or foolish talk; a variant spelling of baloney.

clue.text: Vote is rigged in local council

indicators.note: an election that is rigged is fixed, so these letters are manipulated into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that the ballot for the town council has been fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Russian usage a soviet was an elected council, local or higher, in the USSR.

clue.text: Maestro's original story about one with university background

indicators.note: the original of a word is its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a lie is a made-up story; about here loosely ties the story to the one it concerns

explanation.surface: A conductor's first tale concerns someone with an academic past.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's social surroundings or environment, the setting they come from.

clue.text: One rendering 'Gosh!' to reptile that's unusual?

definitions.text: One rendering 'Gosh!' to reptile that's unusual?

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, signalling these letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone who exclaims in surprise at a strange lizard or snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue doubles as definition: a person who studies reptiles might well exclaim at an unusual specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist whose field is the study of reptiles and amphibians might exclaim over an odd specimen.

clue.text: She had orrises, peculiar plants

indicators.note: peculiar means strange or odd, so the letters are made into something odd

explanation.surface: A gardener's border full of iris roots looks strange.
explanation.walkthrough: Orrises are irises grown for their fragrant roots, which neatly keeps the surface in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent-rooted members of the cabbage family, grown to make a sharp condiment.

clue.text: What brings comrades together? Fantastic mountain rides

indicators.note: fantastic means wild or fanciful, so these letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A trekking holiday with great rides in the hills bonds companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comrades' is the leftist form of address, so the cause that unites workers is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Organised labour movement joining workers, often addressed as comrades, in collective bargaining.

clue.text: Found drug in packing case

indicators.note: the drug is put in, packed within the case

parts.note: a crate is a packing case
E is shorthand for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Narcotics discovered inside a shipping container.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something is to establish or bring it into existence.

clue.text: Native in old garb at home meeting a lecturer

parts.note: rig is clothing, an outfit
in means at home

explanation.surface: An indigenous person in traditional dress welcomes an academic at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Original inhabitants are the first or native ones, indigenous to a place.

clue.text: Looking ill, wish for having early termination

indicators.note: the word is ended early, losing its final letter

parts.note: want means wish for

explanation.surface: Someone pale who longs for an early end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale and sickly in appearance, pallid from illness or tiredness.

clue.text: Queen in Canadian capital

definitions.meaning: the Latin word for queen, used in royal titles
the capital city of the province of Saskatchewan

explanation.surface: A monarch visiting Ottawa or another Canadian seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for a reigning female monarch, and the name of Saskatchewan's provincial capital.

clue.text: Was keen to finish, having so little energy inside

indicators.note: inside means the following pieces are put within the finish

parts.note: end means finish
thus means so, therefore
E is the physics symbol for energy, a little of the word

explanation.surface: Someone eager to be done though they have almost no stamina left.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been eager or excited about something, past tense of a verb of enthusiasm.

clue.text: House has no place for unserviceable tool

indicators.note: having no place for something means it is removed

parts.note: U/S is the military and engineering abbreviation for unserviceable

explanation.surface: A home without room for broken garden implements.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden implement with a blade on a long handle used for weeding.

clue.text: Artificial hair worn by loony

indicators.note: the hair is worn round the loony, so it wraps the other piece

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair
mad means loony, crazy

explanation.surface: A synthetic wig worn by an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Made by people rather than occurring in nature, synthetic.

clue.text: Drink lacking colour, without head

indicators.note: without its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: pale means lacking colour, wan

explanation.surface: A colourless beverage with no froth on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer, especially a traditional British brewed beverage served in pubs.

clue.text: Put on an act before nurse

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: Someone performing ahead of a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To make believe or feign, behaving as if something were true.

clue.text: Writer and artist is entertaining Adam's lad

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
Abel was a son of Adam in the Book of Genesis
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author and a painter host the son of the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the French Renaissance author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: Nymph interrupting hill fighter

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
an oread is a mountain nymph in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A spirit of the woods breaks into a hillside battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter, especially one on horseback, in Spanish tradition.

clue.text: Make more of the last bit of food with stew

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a ragout is a highly seasoned meat stew

explanation.surface: Stretching out the end of a meal with a casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract or prolong something, making it last longer than needed.

clue.text: The Circle Line?

parts.note: not the London Underground route but a straight line drawn across a circle through its centre

explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route; read literally it is a line in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight segment passing through a circle's centre from edge to edge.

clue.text: Spoil that short girl

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Ruin that brief young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Overdrawn after holiday? Support needed

indicators.note: after places the overdrawn piece following the holiday

parts.note: a trip is a holiday or excursion
OD is the bank abbreviation for overdrawn

explanation.surface: Back from a vacation in the red and needing financial help.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-legged stand, used to steady a camera or other equipment.

clue.text: Pub quarrel in Cumbrian town

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A dispute breaks out in a pub in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: BARROW-in-Furness is a shipbuilding town in Cumbria, the county of north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrow-in-Furness, a port and shipbuilding town in north-west England.

clue.text: A church that's 'wicked'!

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A place of worship declared sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' here is slang for brilliant, not evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang terms of approval meaning excellent or great.

clue.text: Cleaning the house and getting black?

definitions.meaning: doing paid domestic cleaning work, as a char or cleaning lady does
scorching or burning something until it is blackened

explanation.walkthrough: A char is British slang for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a char's household work, and scorching something until blackened, are both senses.

clue.text: Daniel's new introductory section

indicators.note: new means remade, so these letters are formed afresh

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A man named Daniel has a fresh opening chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening passage leading into the main part of a programme or text.

clue.text: Dress that goes across the classes

definitions.text: Dress that goes across the classes

parts.words: Dress that goes across the classes
parts.note: sounds like clothing worn by every social class, but really attire worn throughout the forms of a school

explanation.walkthrough: 'Classes' suggests social strata; it means school classes, each pupil dressed alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard clothing all pupils of a school are required to wear.
